newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico blue-chip stocks finish at record high.
newsitem.headline: Mexico blue-chip stocks finish at record high.

text.p: Mexican blue-chip stocks closed at record high on Friday after retreating from their peaks earlier in the session, dealers said.
The IPC index of 37 leading shares rose 16.13 points, or 0.36 percent, to finish at 4,481.11, on trading of 117.15 million shares.
Earlier, the IPC crossed a psychological barrier, rising as high as 4,505.36 points before slipping back.
"There was a little, very healthy profit-taking, but the trend continues to be positive," Javier Gutierrez, director of analysis at BBV-Probursa brokerage, said.
Gutierrez said the advance reflected positive economic trends in Mexico and the United States and expectations of declining interest rates in the second half of the year.
"Various foreigners entered the market. It appeared that they were changing from Brazil to here," one dealer said.
Traders said month-end demand for liquidity prompted some of the profit-taking, leading the IPC to retreat from its earlier highs.
Gainers include Sidek B rose 11.32 percent, Grupo Financiero Inbursa series B shares gained 9.03 percent and Grupo Corvi climbed 6.07 percent.

Shares from the largest companies, such as Banamex-Accival, Grupo Financiero Bancomer and Telmex lost ground. Banacci series B shares fell 1.61 percent, Bancomer series B shares dropped 1.75 percent and Telmex shed 0.6 percent.
